title: Backpressure with a bounded mpsc channel
summary: Replace an unbounded channel that eats memory with mpsc::channel, then find the receive loop never ends because the original tx is still alive.

turns.user: feeding it a big csv grows memory to several GB and it gets OOM killed. yes i know inserts are slow. also the files come split into parts now, read them all at once

assistant.body: TL;DR: the unbounded_channel is the leak. Its send succeeds no matter how far behind the receiver is, so every line the reader gets ahead of insert sits in the queue. With mpsc::channel(1024), send().await waits once the queue is full, which slows the reader down to the speed of insert. That is backpressure. If the receiver goes away first, send returns Err and the reader stops. For the split files, each one gets its own clone of tx and its own task. This should work as expected.

turns.user: everything looks read but import never returns. logs just stop

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous version kept the original tx alive for the whole function. recv only returns None once every Sender has been dropped. Each task drops its clone when it finishes, but the one it was cloned from is still in scope, so the channel never closes and the loop waits for a line that will never come. Dropping tx right before the loop fixes it.

turns.user: fixed. rows are really wide though, 1024 is still heavy. make it 64

assistant.body: Makes sense. The capacity is the most lines held in memory at once, so wide rows are a good reason to shrink it. As long as insert is the slow side, 64 costs no throughput.
